cases.result: V0.5 selector chooses a minimum-incidence root with d<=2; the existing low-incidence proof gives N'<=N-4<=41 and strong induction enters the proved N<=44 frontier.

r9_cell_derivation: Hard-region assumptions require m>=5 and L>=27, hence m<=8.

selector_degree_bound.statement: In every r=9 hard cell, v0.5 selects a root with d_min<=floor(L/9)<=3.
cases: If d_min<=2, the already-proved low-incidence N-minus-4 reroot applies to the actually executed pivot.
If d_min=3, the actually executed pivot has incidence exactly 3.

selected_degree3_raw_bound.statement: For every selected degree-3 root pivot in an N45 hard cell, exact ordinary elimination is raw-cap safe and produces state_units<=40.
proof: At the root s=1+m+L=36 and there are r=9 live variables.
A pure degree-3 pivot has an empty polarity bucket and is deletion-only.
A mixed degree-3 pivot has polarity split {1,2}.
For split p=1,q=2 the existing generic bound is B_x=s-4+U_singleton; the symmetric split is identical.
The singleton bucket contains one canonical clause whose nonpivot tail has width at most r-1=8, so U_singleton<=8.

finite_frontier_theorem.name: V0_5_PROOF_SELECTOR_NO_RAW_CAP_RESCUE_REQUIRED_THROUGH_N45
finite_frontier_theorem.statement: Inherit the proved N<=44 v0.5 frontier. At N=45, m<=4 roots are covered by the small-clause invariant; m>=5,L<3r roots are constructively rerouted by the v0.5 minimum-incidence selector; m>=5,L>=3r implies r<=9. The r<=8 region is below cap by the existing exact recurrence. The only r=9 cells are (5,30),(6,29),(7,28),(8,27); the selector chooses d<=3, with d<=2 rerouting into the old frontier and d=3 having generic raw bound <=40 followed by a tail whose maximum raw bound is 85747/64<2025. Therefore the candidate has ordinary exact cap-safe continuation throughout every legitimate N<=45 root covered by these finite structural cases, without invoking v2/v3 due to raw-cap unavailability.
